assumptions.choice: Exit short when close crosses above SMA(20) OR trailing stop is hit (close >= trail_stop)
assumptions.reason: The spec explicitly defines only the long exit rule. The symmetric rule is the only literal reading consistent with the described ratcheting short trail_stop, which is otherwise unused without a corresponding exit trigger.

assumptions.choice: Trailing stop checked via equivalent in-next() logic (comparing close to trail_stop each bar and calling self.close() on trigger) rather than native backtrader stop orders updated each bar
assumptions.reason: The spec explicitly permits 'equivalent logic in next()'. Using cancel-and-replace stop orders each bar risks execution artefacts with backtrader's order queue; the in-next() approach is behaviourally equivalent on bar-close data.

assumptions.choice: Inclusive comparison: long exit if close <= trail_stop; short exit if close >= trail_stop
assumptions.reason: Spec says 'when trailing stop is hit'; equality (close exactly at stop) constitutes a hit.

assumptions.choice: highest_close and trail_stop are initialised on the first close bar after position opens (i.e., the open-execution bar's close)
assumptions.reason: Entry executes at the next bar's open; the first available close thereafter is the logical start of 'highest/lowest close since entry'.

assumptions.choice: Strict inequalities: cross_above requires prev_close < prev_sma AND close > sma; cross_below requires prev_close > prev_sma AND close < sma
assumptions.reason: Spec uses 'crosses above/below' implying a strict transition; bars exactly on SMA do not constitute a cross in either direction.

assumptions.choice: Commission configured by harness (0.001); no additional slippage beyond backtrader default (none)
assumptions.reason: Spec says 'include commission/slippage placeholders'; commission is set externally by the harness, and backtrader has no built-in slippage by default. No slippage model is specified.

assumptions.choice: When a position is closed due to a crossover signal, no opposite entry is placed on the same bar
assumptions.reason: The single pending-order guard (self.order) prevents placing a new entry while the close order is pending. The crossover that triggers the exit is already 'consumed'; a fresh signal on the next bar is required to enter the opposite direction.
